newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Novoship eyes role transporting CPC oil.
newsitem.headline: Russian Novoship eyes role transporting CPC oil.

text.p: Russian Novorossiiskoye Morskoye Parokhodstvo (Novoship) said it plans to become the main transporter of oil from the Caspian Pipeline Consortium's (CPC) pipeline terminal on the Black Sea, where it is based.
"Our ships could be the ones which transport oil from the Yuzhnaya Ozereika terminal," said company president Leonid Loza, referring to the Black Sea port where the pipeline will end.
"It is only plans, but development and discussion of them have begun," said vice-president Sergei Terekhin. He said Novoship had contacted a number of Western oil majors on the project.
The CPC is a project by Western and Russian oil majors to transport oil from western Kazakhstan to Novorossiisk.
Novoship has commissioned four 106,000-tonne capacity tankers from Japan's NKK Corp for delivery beginning in November 1998.
The tankers would arrive in time for the pipeline consortium's projected opening in September 1999 and would give Novoship the capacity to ship the oil, company managers said.
Novoship transported 42.5 million tonnes of cargo in 1996, up from 38.6 in 1995.

The company, which as of May 16 owned 90 ships with an average age of 12.2 years and a total capacity of 4.2 million tonnes, posted a $36.5 million loss last year, according to international standard accounts by Coopers & Lybrand.
